English: library on the left, inspector on the right; timeline stays LTR in both languages

visual baselines: screenshots match the committed baselines (SSIM ≥ 0.98), or were written on first run

source viewer: opens from the library by keyboard, shows the file's own frames (0, 30, 71 by barcode), plays; I and O mark a range of 42 frames; "add" places exactly that range at the end of the timeline as one transaction (picture + linked sound) and the timeline then shows source frames 30 and 71 at its first and last frame; shortcuts typed in the viewer do not move the timeline behind it; focus returns to the button

"insert at the playhead" from the source viewer is one transaction: the clip under the playhead is split there, the 20-frame range sits in the gap, everything later moves 20 frames, and the timeline shows the frames in order (…, before the cut, the inserted 100–119, then the continuation)

"overwrite at the playhead" replaces exactly the range's length on the picture and sound tracks in one transaction: the timeline keeps its length, nothing later moves, and it shows the new frames 60–69 followed by what was already there (110–119, then the continuation)

timeline target tracks: with ◎ pressed on a picture track and a sound track, "add to timeline" puts the file's picture and sound on those tracks and a paste of the copied picture clip puts the copy on the target picture track (the sound clip was not selected, so it is not copied); every other track is untouched

source viewer target tracks: with a picture track and a sound track chosen, "overwrite" puts the range (source 20–29) on exactly those tracks at the playhead in one transaction, leaves every other track as it was, and the frame there now shows the new picture on top; undo and removing the two tracks restore the timeline

dragging a file from the library onto a picture track puts it on that track at the frame under the pointer (within one frame), with its linked sound, in one transaction; the drop marker goes away; undo removes it
a file dropped from the computer onto a picture track is imported into the library and placed on that track at the frame under the pointer (within one frame)
two files dropped together are both imported and placed one after the other in name order, the first at the frame under the pointer
slip by keyboard (three single frames and one step of ten): the selected clip keeps its place and length and now shows source 73–82; its neighbours are unchanged

roll by keyboard: the cut before the selected clip moves two frames later (the earlier clip plays two frames more, the selected clip starts two frames later with the same picture at every other frame), the timeline keeps its length, and rolling back restores it

roll by dragging: Ctrl + dragging the start edge of a clip two frames later moves the cut exactly as the keyboard roll does, in one transaction, without changing the timeline length; one undo restores it

slide by keyboard: three presses move the selected clip three frames later between its neighbours (same ten pictures; the clip before it plays three frames more, the clip after it starts three frames later), the timeline keeps its length, and sliding back restores it
slide by dragging: Ctrl + dragging the clip three frames later gives the same frames as three keyboard slides, in one transaction, with the timeline length unchanged; one undo restores it

"play backwards" in the Inspector: the clip keeps its place and length and its ten frames now show source 82 down to 73 on server stills (neighbours unchanged), the paused preview shows the same frame as the still, an exported file of that stretch shows the same twelve frames in the same order, the clip is marked on the timeline, and unchecking restores 73…82
"detach picture from sound" in the Inspector unlinks the selected picture clip and its sound clip in one transaction; the button is then no longer offered

track buttons: hiding a picture track removes its picture from the server still and marks the track; showing it restores the same frame; locking marks the track and an edit to its clips is refused (API and Delete key in the editor); unlocking clears it

editor: a track is added from the timeline; a track and a library file are renamed in place (Hebrew + Latin), Enter commits and focus returns to the rename button, Escape discards; three transactions in all
editor: the project is renamed in the header; "clear all keyframes" removes a clip's animation; "remove empty tracks" from the palette removes the empty track added earlier, in one transaction each

"move track up" from the palette swaps the selected clip's track with the one above it in the list, the timeline rows before and after are exactly the lane order of that list (titles, captions, picture stack front-most first, sound in list order), and Ctrl+Z restores the order
proof ran to completion
